sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), observe an independent sample \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) from the row law \(P_n\in\mathcal M\); rows may vary arbitrarily with \(n\).
sampling_model.units: The number of multinomial atoms \(|\mathcal J|\) is fixed, while their probabilities may vanish with \(n\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument and treatment are binary; the outcome has the fixed ordered support \(\mathcal Y\), and selection is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The inferential class strengthens the inherited pointwise model only by fixed uniform bounds \(\epsilon\le P_n(Z=1\mid X=x)\le1-\epsilon\) and \(M(p_n)\ge m_*\); individual cells and cut gaps may vanish.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical atom vector \(\widehat p_n\) is the sole first-stage estimator. Algebraic division is totalized by \(u\oslash0=0\), the endpoint center uses \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)=(0,1)\) at zero aggregate empirical mass, and \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\) when that fallback is invoked or the legal base set is empty. The common Gaussian draw is realized through the principal covariance square root, and its measurable critical value uses the lower-quantile convention. No support screening, variance floor, or deterministic calibration guard is used.

body.tldr: The accepted sharp-identification theorem continues to give \(\Theta_I(p)=[L(p),U(p)]\).  The round-two oriented repair passes the accepted \(K=4\) singleton-cell parity test: an explicit one-sided ray envelope has \(W(g)=0\) and \(W(-g)>0\), and a legal survivor-to-never-selected donor transfer dominates the witness's exact finite endpoint increment.  This shows that the earlier contradiction was caused by the even statistic \(\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}z|\), not by orientation itself.  The all-array theorem nevertheless remains unproved because no global row-by-row proof of oriented legal-envelope domination, covariance traction, and relative lower-quantile transfer has been established at simultaneous capacity, selection-total, and cut faces.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent settles sharp identification for the finite ordered survivor-complier benefit interval.  Existing inference results either impose fixed-law differentiability, start from supplied asymptotically linear endpoint or standardized moment representations, or require geometric and positive-variance regularity that excludes changing support and a jointly collapsing endpoint scale.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary-instrument model permits exact capacity geometry and common multinomial Gaussian calibration, but legality makes the local derivative envelope intrinsically oriented at binding selection-total faces.  The explicit \(K=4\) calculation now distinguishes this one-sided issue from the separate simultaneous-face and relative-quantile problems.
project_justification.fill: This round supplies an explicit oriented parity and finite-curvature certificate on the previously fatal singleton-cell witness.  It does not claim uniform coverage: the remaining contribution would require a complete finite legal transfer matrix proving pointwise oriented domination and scale-relative covariance traction through every simultaneous face, followed by a non-even lower-quantile theorem.  No support, cut-gap, cell-mass, or variance floor, screening rule, or deterministic guard is introduced.

body.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith survivor-complier benefit result supplies the exact sharp endpoint formula and full-law sharpness; identification is imported rather than reproved.  Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and no defiers, while Dong and Heiler (2026) support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity.  The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) denominator floor are uniform-class strengthenings here.  Fang and Santos (2019) and Hong and Li (2018) explain derivative-resampling methods, but their generic results do not construct the required nearby legal observed laws.  Frandsen and Pond (2025), Imai and Okamoto (2026), and Andrews and Guggenberger (2009) begin from regular or standardized representations that do not resolve the present one-sided legal-face problem.  The old scale-free unsigned-Gaussian lemma does not establish anti-concentration or quantile transfer for the required non-even maximum.  The new certificate only verifies the oriented mechanism on one explicit legal face and is not a substitute for that global theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The symmetric probe failure is repaired on its original \(K=4\) witness by an explicit oriented ray and legal latent transfer.  The unresolved obstruction is now the simultaneous-face certificate.  At raw-capacity zeros, selection-total ties, and tied threshold cuts, a candidate signed face row can be canceled by other active numerator or denominator terms outside its originating directional cone; consequently its positive part is not automatically pointwise below \(E_{p,r}\).  Donor transfers also alter two capacity margins, so covariance traction cannot be inferred from an abstract spanning argument.  Until every such row is legalized and the non-even Gaussian lower quantile is transferred at relative scale, the uniform theorem and exact-zero-scale branch remain open.
body.honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from the accepted parent and is not a contribution of this note.  The separated regular-face calibration, root-\(n\) width calculations, and diagnostic arrays are not overturned.  This round proves only that the explicit singleton-cell counterexample is compatible with an oriented repair, including exact nearby-legal-base domination of its finite increment.  It does not prove the global oriented comparison or all-array uniform joint coverage.  No individual support, survivor-cell, cut-gap, or variance floor and no screening or deterministic guard has been added.
body.interpretation: The proposed rectangle targets simultaneous coverage of the observed-law sharp endpoint pair \(\Phi(p_n)=(L(p_n),U(p_n))\); it does not redefine the causal probability \(\theta_B\).  The imported identification theorem continues to yield \(\Theta_I(p_n)=[L(p_n),U(p_n)]\).  Exact common-Gaussian calibration on separated regular faces and the existing width calculations remain distinct results.  On the accepted boundary witness, orientation correctly distinguishes a legally inward flat direction from the opposite endpoint-changing direction, but this local success does not establish honesty over arbitrary triangular arrays.
